module_intro: Subtopics: External & Internal Ranges, Nested Construction, Controlling Range Selection, Premium/Discount in Delivery Context.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Module 1 (Institutional Price Delivery Framework) and the full Intermediate volume. This module does not re-teach basic equilibrium or premium/discount definitions. It locates the delivery narrative of Module 1 inside nested dealing ranges and trains selection of the controlling range.
module_objectives: Construct dealing ranges on multiple timeframes and state which range is currently controlling the narrative.
Distinguish external range liquidity (ERL) from internal range liquidity (IRL) relative to a chosen dealing range.
Map a delivery leg (Module 1) onto the premium/discount structure of the controlling range.
Recognise range expansion and contraction as changes in the active container rather than as isolated volatility events.
Handle nested and multiple simultaneous dealing ranges without narrative conflict.
Update or retire a dealing range when external structure expands and holds.
Select PD arrays and liquidity objectives that are consistent with the controlling range's premium/discount filter.
Identify the highest-timeframe range that still frames the active liquidity objective (monthly or weekly for swing narratives; daily for intraday).
Confirm that both boundaries are structurally or liquidity-validated.
Locate equilibrium and label premium / discount.
State the current delivery objective (Module 1) relative to that range: which pool is being sought, and is price in the correct half to support the intended direction?
Identify the next lower-timeframe range that will supply the entry PD arrays and the conditioning sequence.
If the lower-timeframe range's premium/discount conflicts with the controlling range, require additional confluence or stand aside.
Update the controlling range when expansion beyond a boundary holds and a new structural extreme is accepted.

concepts.name: Dealing Range as the Container of Delivery
concepts.definition: Module 1 established that price is delivered from one liquidity pool to another. The dealing range is the price container inside which that delivery is measured. Equilibrium divides the container into premium and discount; those halves filter which PD arrays are high-probability participants in the current delivery leg.

Equilibrium divides the container into premium and discount; those halves filter which PD arrays are high-probability participants in the current delivery leg.

raw_sections.Construction Rule (Advanced):
A dealing range is bounded by a swing high and a swing low that are themselves significant: each has either swept prior liquidity or produced a structural break (BOS / MSS). Arbitrary candle extremes are not ranges.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - Dealing range, equilibrium, premium and discount are core ICT. The requirement that boundaries be structurally or liquidity-validated is consistent with primary teaching and Intermediate refinement.*

concepts.name: External Range vs Internal Range
concepts.definition: External Range Liquidity sits outside the current dealing-range boundaries - above the range high (buy-side) and below the range low (sell-side). ERL is the typical final destination of a completed delivery leg that expands the range or leaves it.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: External Range Liquidity sits outside the current dealing-range boundaries - above the range high (buy-side) and below the range low (sell-side). ERL is the typical final destination of a completed delivery leg that expands the range or leaves it.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.External Range Liquidity (ERL): External Range Liquidity sits outside the current dealing-range boundaries - above the range high (buy-side) and below the range low (sell-side). ERL is the typical final destination of a completed delivery leg that expands the range or leaves it.
raw_sections.Internal Range Liquidity (IRL): Internal Range Liquidity sits inside the dealing range. It includes internal swing points, equal highs/lows inside the range, and, importantly in ICT usage, imbalances (FVGs) that form within the range. IRL often supplies intermediate targets and the PD arrays used for entry during retracement phases of delivery.
raw_sections.Delivery Implication:
A common high-quality sequence is: raid of IRL or of the opposing range boundary -> displacement -> retracement into an internal PD array -> continuation toward ERL. The advanced student always knows whether the current objective is still internal or has become external.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - IRL / ERL distinction is explicitly used in ICT teaching relative to the dealing range.*

concepts.name: Nested Dealing Ranges
concepts.definition: Dealing ranges nest. A monthly range contains weekly ranges; a weekly range contains daily ranges; a daily range contains session or 1-hour ranges. Each lower-timeframe range is a refinement of delivery inside the higher-timeframe container.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Dealing ranges nest. A monthly range contains weekly ranges; a weekly range contains daily ranges; a daily range contains session or 1-hour ranges. Each lower-timeframe range is a refinement of delivery inside the higher-timeframe container.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.Fractal Construction: Dealing ranges nest. A monthly range contains weekly ranges; a weekly range contains daily ranges; a daily range contains session or 1-hour ranges. Each lower-timeframe range is a refinement of delivery inside the higher-timeframe container.
raw_sections.Controlling Range: The controlling range is the highest-timeframe range that still constrains the current narrative. When weekly and daily ranges agree on premium/discount location relative to the intended delivery direction, confluence is high. When they conflict, the higher-timeframe range retains priority for bias; the lower-timeframe range is used only for timing.
raw_sections.Practical Rule: Before selecting any PD array or entry model, state the controlling range and whether price is in its premium or discount half. Then state the next lower range that will be used for execution refinement.

concepts.name: Multiple Simultaneous Ranges
concepts.definition: At any moment several ranges may be active: a weekly range still being delivered, a daily range that has just expanded, and a session range that is consolidating. The advanced task is to rank them by narrative authority, not to treat them as equal.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: At any moment several ranges may be active: a weekly range still being delivered, a daily range that has just expanded, and a session range that is consolidating. The advanced task is to rank them by narrative authority, not to treat them as equal.

raw_sections.Recognition: At any moment several ranges may be active: a weekly range still being delivered, a daily range that has just expanded, and a session range that is consolidating. The advanced task is to rank them by narrative authority, not to treat them as equal.
raw_sections.Selection Discipline: Authority flows from higher timeframe to lower. A session-range discount long that sits in weekly premium is fighting the controlling narrative unless the weekly delivery has itself failed.

concepts.name: Range Expansion and Contraction in Delivery Context
concepts.definition: Range expansion occurs when price leaves the current boundaries with displacement and the new extreme holds. The old range is retired or becomes internal to a new, larger container. Expansion is often the visible completion of a delivery leg toward prior ERL, which then becomes the new boundary.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Range expansion occurs when price leaves the current boundaries with displacement and the new extreme holds. The old range is retired or becomes internal to a new, larger container. Expansion is often the visible completion of a delivery leg toward prior ERL, which then becomes the new boundary.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.Expansion: Range expansion occurs when price leaves the current boundaries with displacement and the new extreme holds. The old range is retired or becomes internal to a new, larger container. Expansion is often the visible completion of a delivery leg toward prior ERL, which then becomes the new boundary.
raw_sections.Contraction: Range contraction is the formation of a tighter container inside the larger range. It is the typical environment in which the next manipulation and expansion are prepared. Prolonged contraction without displacement is not an invitation to force trades; it is a signal that delivery has not yet resumed.
raw_sections.Link to Module 1 Conditions: Consolidation often coincides with contraction or with a stable range. Expansion is the delivery condition that creates new range boundaries. Retracement occurs inside the range. Reversal may expand the range in the opposite direction and redefine the container.

concepts.name: Premium / Discount as Delivery Filters
concepts.definition: Premium and discount are not static labels; they are filters on participation in the current delivery leg. When the higher-timeframe delivery is bullish, long PD arrays are preferentially sought in discount of the controlling range. When the delivery is bearish, short PD arrays are preferentially sought in premium.

raw_sections.Advanced Application: Premium and discount are not static labels; they are filters on participation in the current delivery leg. When the higher-timeframe delivery is bullish, long PD arrays are preferentially sought in discount of the controlling range. When the delivery is bearish, short PD arrays are preferentially sought in premium.
raw_sections.Wrong-Half Participation: A technically perfect bullish Order Block or FVG that sits in deep premium of the controlling range is participating against the location filter. It may still work if higher-timeframe confluence is overwhelming, but it is lower probability and requires stronger displacement and structural confirmation.
raw_sections.Target Symmetry: In a bullish delivery the premium half of the range (and ultimately the ERL above the range high) is the natural target territory. In a bearish delivery the discount half and the ERL below the range low serve the same role.

concepts.name: Selecting the Controlling Range - Procedure
concepts.definition:
- Identify the highest-timeframe range that still frames the active liquidity objective (monthly or weekly for swing narratives; daily for intraday).

- Confirm that both boundaries are structurally or liquidity-validated.

- Locate equilibrium and label premium / discount.

- State the current delivery objective (Module 1) relative to that range: which pool is being sought, and is price in the correct half to support the intended direction?

- Identify the next lower-timeframe range that will supply the entry PD arrays and the conditioning sequence.

- If the lower-timeframe range's premium/discount conflicts with the controlling range, require additional confluence or stand aside.

- Update the controlling range when expansion beyond a boundary holds and a new structural extreme is accepted.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Narrative - Nested Ranges in Delivery
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
Weekly controlling range: 1.0500 - 1.1200, equilibrium 1.0850. Price is at 1.0620 (discount). Weekly delivery objective is buy-side liquidity above 1.1200.

Daily range nested inside: 1.0550 - 1.0800, equilibrium 1.0675. Price has just swept the daily low and displaced higher, leaving a daily FVG in discount of both the daily and the weekly range.

Session range: consolidating inside the daily FVG. London produces a further sell-side raid and a bullish MSS.

Narrative statement: "Weekly delivery is seeking the external buy-side pool above 1.1200. Price is in weekly and daily discount. The daily displacement FVG, reinforced by London conditioning, supplies the entry. Intermediate targets are daily internal buy-side pools; the final objective remains weekly ERL."

This is range-aligned, multi-timeframe delivery. A long taken from a premium daily array while the weekly remained in discount would have been range-misaligned.

failure_conditions.name: Failure and Range Retirement
failure_conditions.definition:
A dealing range is retired or expanded when:

994. Price closes beyond a boundary with displacement and the new extreme holds as structure.

995. The liquidity objective that defined the range has been satisfied and a new opposing objective takes control.

996. Higher-timeframe structure invalidates the premise that justified the range.

After retirement, the new boundaries are drawn and the premium/discount filter is recalculated. Continuing to use a retired range produces narrative lag.

common_misinterpretations.name: Common Misinterpretations
common_misinterpretations.definition:
997. Treating every swing high/low as a dealing-range boundary without structural or liquidity validation.

998. Allowing a lower-timeframe range's premium/discount to override the controlling higher-timeframe range.

999. Entering long from deep premium (or short from deep discount) of the controlling range because a lower-timeframe signal appeared.

1000. Failing to update the range after a genuine expansion, so that premium/discount labels become outdated.

1001. Confusing IRL with ERL and therefore mis-stating whether the current delivery objective is intermediate or final.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
Dealing range, equilibrium, premium and discount are foundational ICT. The IRL / ERL distinction relative to the range is explicitly taught. Nested ranges follow from the fractal character of ICT structure and are demonstrated in multi-timeframe examples. The discipline of selecting a controlling range and subordinating lower-timeframe location to it is the advanced operational synthesis required for consistent narrative construction.

***Source / Research note:** Primary orientation: ICT teaching on dealing ranges, premium/discount, and liquidity relative to range boundaries. IRL/ERL language is used in ICT material. Nested-range application is the consistent multi-timeframe extension of those teachings. Community refinements of selection checklists are used only where they align with primary logic.*

rules.statement: Selecting the controlling range procedure: (1) identify the highest-timeframe range that still frames the active liquidity objective (monthly or weekly for swing narratives; daily for intraday); (2) confirm both boundaries are structurally or liquidity-validated; (3) locate equilibrium and label premium/discount; (4) state the current delivery objective relative to that range (which pool is sought, is price in the correct half); (5) identify the next lower-timeframe range that will supply the entry PD arrays and conditioning sequence; (6) if the lower-timeframe range's premium/discount conflicts with the controlling range, require additional confluence or stand aside; (7) update the controlling range when expansion beyond a boundary holds and a new structural extreme is accepted.

When multiple ranges are simultaneously active (e.g. a weekly range still being delivered, a daily range that just expanded, a session range consolidating), rank them by narrative authority rather than treating them as equal. Authority flows from higher timeframe to lower: a session-range discount long that sits in weekly premium is fighting the controlling narrative unless the weekly delivery has itself failed.

A dealing range is retired or expanded when: (1) price closes beyond a boundary with displacement and the new extreme holds as structure; (2) the liquidity objective that defined the range has been satisfied and a new opposing objective takes control; (3) higher-timeframe structure invalidates the premise that justified the range. After retirement, new boundaries are drawn and the premium/discount filter is recalculated; continuing to use a retired range produces narrative lag.
applies_to: Range Expansion and Contraction in Delivery Context

no_trade_conditions.statement: If a lower-timeframe range's premium/discount location conflicts with the controlling higher-timeframe range, require additional confluence or stand aside rather than entering long from deep premium (or short from deep discount) of the controlling range purely because a lower-timeframe signal appeared.

key_terms: Controlling range - the highest-timeframe dealing range that still governs the active narrative.
External Range Liquidity (ERL) - liquidity outside the range boundaries; typical final delivery objective.
Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) - liquidity and imbalances inside the range; intermediate targets and entry arrays.
Nested ranges - lower-timeframe dealing ranges contained inside higher-timeframe ranges.
Range expansion - displacement beyond a boundary that holds and redefines the container.
Range contraction - formation of a tighter container inside a larger range; often preparatory.
self_test_questions: What distinguishes a valid dealing-range boundary from an arbitrary swing?
How should a conflict between daily discount and weekly premium be resolved for bias?
Where does ERL sit relative to the dealing range, and what is its typical role in delivery?
When must the controlling range be updated?
Why is a bullish PD array in deep premium of the controlling range lower probability?
